newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday August 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday August 6.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Massimo D'Alema, leader of the largest party in the centre-left governing coalition, made a first trip to the Vatican last week. A meeting with Pope John Paul may now be on the cards. (La Repubblica)

* Former star anti-graft magistrate, Antonio Di Pietro, said he will withdraw his controversial candidature for a place in Italy's senate if the governing Olive Tree coalition chooses veteran journalist Alessandro Curzi as its official candidate. (all)

* Italian oil producers agreed to block petrol price rises for eight days after Prime Minister Romano Prodi complained that current rates were too high. Prices have been pushed up by sharp rises in the dollar. (all)

* The Italian cabinet has approved two decree laws to tighten up laws on Value Added Tax (VAT) payments. The new laws will make it more difficult for firms to avoid paying indirect taxes on purchases for personal use and will bring Italy in line with European Union directives. (all)
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
